Let

Ct  = total (stoichiometric) calcium  = 0.020 M  
Et  = total EDTA (same)               = 0.020 M  

At the start all Ca and EDTA are present as the 1 : 1 complex CaEDTA⁻².

Dissociation equilibrium  
CaEDTA²⁻  ⇌  Ca²⁺  +  EDTA⁴⁻

Let x = [Ca²⁺] at equilibrium (the same amount of free EDTA⁴⁻ will be produced).

[CaEDTA²⁻] = 0.020 – x  
[Ca²⁺]     = x  
[EDTA⁴⁻]   = x

Formation (stability) constant  
Kf = [CaEDTA²⁻] / ([Ca²⁺][EDTA⁴⁻]) = 5 × 10¹⁰

Insert the equilibrium concentrations:

5 × 10¹⁰ = (0.020 – x)/(x²)

Because Kf is very large, dissociation is slight, so x ≪ 0.020 and 0.020 – x ≈ 0.020:

5 × 10¹⁰ ≈ 0.020 / x²

Solve for x:

x² ≈ 0.020 / (5 × 10¹⁰)  
x² ≈ 4 × 10⁻¹³  
x ≈ √(4 × 10⁻¹³) ≈ 2 × 10⁻⁶.⁵ ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M

Thus the equilibrium concentration of free Ca²⁺ is 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M.

Answer: D
